title: MUniverse Avrillon et al 2024
description: High-density surface electromyography (HDsEMG) recordings from 16 young participants performing isometric ankle dorsiflexions or knee extensions at submaximal force levels (10-80% MVC). EMG signals were acquired using four 64-electrode arrays (256 total electrodes) positioned over the tibialis anterior or vastus lateralis muscles. This dataset enables investigation of motor unit recruitment and rate coding properties across diverse neuromodulatory inputs during sustained muscle contractions.
methods_description: HDsEMG signals were recorded from either the tibialis anterior (TA) or vastus lateralis (VL) using four 2D electrode arrays (64 electrodes each; interelectrode spacing: 4 mm for TA, 8 mm for VL). Participants performed isometric contractions at 10-80% MVC. For ankle dorsiflexions, the foot was fixed to an ankle dynamometer; for knee extensions, participants sat on an instrumented chair with tibia against a rigid resistance. Force was recorded synchronously using load cells and the EMG-Quattrocento acquisition system.
